sections.chapter_title: Controller area network with flexible data rate (FDCAN)
sections.text_helper: Section 71.4.2 "Error management" in chapter 71 (Controller area network with flexible data rate (FDCAN)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 3630.
sections.section_content:
The error management as described in the CAN protocol is handled entirely by hardware
using a transmit error counter (TEC value, in the CAN_ECR register) and a receive error
counter (REC value, in the CAN_ECR register), incremented or decremented according to
the error condition. Both can be read by software to determine the stability of the network.
For detailed information about TEC and REC management, refer to the CAN standard.
Bus-Off recovery
The Bus-Off state is reached when TEC > 255, this state is indicated by the BO bit in the
CAN_PSR register. In Bus-Off state the CAN is no longer able to transmit and receive
messages, it must wait at least for the recovery sequence specified in the CAN standard
(129 occurrences of 11 consecutive recessive bits monitored on FDCAN_RX input).
[Figure 960. CAN error state diagram]
Note: In initialization mode, CAN does not monitor the CAN RX signal, therefore it cannot
complete the recovery sequence. To recover, CAN must be in normal mode.
